  "quiz": "0001",
  "submission": "s2",
  "items": [
    {"id": "q1", "verdict": "correct", "misconception": null, "feedback": "Right. What makes it an agent is the loop: the model picks an action, the program runs it, and the result comes back for the next step."},
    {"id": "q2", "verdict": "correct", "misconception": null, "feedback": "Right. The model only writes a request, like check_calendar(machine=\"laser cutter\", date=\"tomorrow\"); the program around it does the actual calling."},
    {"id": "q3", "verdict": "wrong", "misconception": "M6", "feedback": "Not quite. But if step 40 gets the same failing test as step 1, step 400 will too, so you need a step limit that stops the loop and reports back. For example, a limit of 20 steps would have ended this run after 20 identical edits and handed the bug to a person."},
    {"id": "q4", "verdict": "partial", "misconception": "M4", "feedback": "Partly right. 4 is the correct count: three tool requests plus the final answer. The off part is your reason, 'it runs check_calendar, then search_manuals...': the model never runs tools, it only requests them and the program runs them. So the calls are: question in, request 1 out; result 1 in, request 2 out; result 2 in, request 3 out; result 3 in, final answer out."},
    {"id": "q5", "verdict": "correct", "misconception": null, "feedback": "Right. The result goes back in as the model's next input, and the model uses it to decide its next step, like the calendar result telling it to go check the manuals next."},
    {"id": "q6", "verdict": "partial", "misconception": null, "feedback": "Partly right. The name is part of it, and check_calendar does hint at calendars. But the model works from the whole tool description the program gives it: name, what the tool does, and its parameters. A tool named do_thing3 with the description 'checks machine bookings for a date' still gets picked correctly, and a nicely named tool with no description is a guess."}
  ],
  "summary": "You have the agent loop down: what makes an agent, what the model outputs, and why results go back in. Work next on who runs the tools (the program, never the model) and on why a loop needs a stopping condition. Reread the part of the agent-loop lesson on stopping conditions, then redo q3 and q6 from memory."
}
EOF
